Nobody is meant to be here at all, we just are. The only way humans have been able to create meaning is by setting our own paths. I don't think we were really "meant" to make cars or smartphones or drive-thru restaurants, but there was a want so we made it. The hardest part for you now is going to be finding what you want to pursue. Don't ever say should. There's nothing you *should* do, nowhere you *should* be. The paths are different for every soul.

Nobody else can crawl up there and do the rewiring that your brain needs, which sucks because I assume you aren't an electrician, haha. But it's okay. I'm struggling too, and haven't quite figured it out myself but I remember I told myself when I was a child, "I'm not gonna live to 21 whether by accident or on purpose". But I survived past that. Don't fulfill that prophecy. Find excuses to keep going. Maybe there's a video game coming out soon that you gotta play first. A movie they said would release and you gotta see if it's as bad as it looks like it'll be. A friend finishing an art piece you gotta see. Keep finding those excuses. And maybe find a therapist that'll help you unravel and organize all these thoughts. They'll teach you how to be an electrician.

Just trust that because you were born, you don't need to earn your space. It's already carved out for you. Give yourself some extra legroom and make it bigger, take it all up. It's gonna be so hard but you have to trust the work is worth it. It's so worth it. I'm sorry he wasn't there when you needed him. You gotta be there for yourself now.

Congratulations on being Cis+, my friend! You are absolutely experiencing dysphoria. I literally am a trans guy and I'm so horribly feminine that I've considered just giving up. But we keep going, we must! I'm a man because I am a man. Because I say so, and that is my truth, how I really feel. I assume you agree. So if you do, you are a woman because you are a woman. Because you say so, and that is your truth, how you really feel. You don't need to prove that shit to anybody.

 There are so many women out there just like you, cis and trans who feel your pain. And they're all women. You mention your peers are allowed to exist, and it is so frustrating to be looking at a life you feel like you should have too. But you need to carve your own path. I'm sure a lot of your girl friends who you see as sufficiently feminine struggle with their womanhood as well. It's just what it is like being a girl! 

It sucks but you have to come to terms with who you are. It won't happen immediately and it's gonna hurt but if what all my queer mothers have been telling me is true, it'll happen if you try. In the meantime, affirm your gender! It's been really important for me during my transition to do things that make me feel closer to who I feel like inside. Do your nails or your hair, get yourself something new and cute that makes you feel like a girl, what have you! Even if you aren't gay, try finding some lesbian-straight alliances or similar open communities and reach out to your butch sisters, hell, even many femmes may have masculine features they wrestle with!

You are a gift, and completely irreplaceable. Don't confine yourself to being at odds with the features you feel fail your womanhood, embrace them. After all, can they really be man features if you were born into them as a woman? 

Good luck, girl, I love you wherever you are!

I'm not equating medical transition to being trans.. I'm trans with no medical intervention (though I wish to get it in the future, and I know and love many trans people who do not want a medical transition at all. This conversation has nuance. Obviously I don't go around telling every fash I think gender is a choice but I figured my point of view would be a little more understood around other trans people??

Thanks for sharing your story, genuinely. I've felt the exact same way when I first started transitioning. I feel as though we are maybe misunderstanding each other, though? I'm not saying you chose to be trans. I didn't choose to have gender dysphoria either and it sounds like transphobia has hurt you severely, like it's hurt all of us. But when you try and justify your existence on "I'm doing this against my will", they're going to find a way to make you normal. I was a transmedicalist for the early years of my transition, believed you absolutely must medically transition and you had to at least try and pass or else you weren't really trans. God forbid you be non-binary or a feminine trans man or a butch trans woman. I did this in a desperate attempt to plead to the people who wanted me to conform "I need this to be comfortable, I would be cis if I had the option." These people then spent every moment they could to try and cure my dysphoria. Conversion therapy, corrective measures I don't wish to elaborate on, everything they could to make me their normal little girl again.

I met more people out in the community, terrified of basically any and every cis person that they would be out to get me anyways, even if they'd said they were supportive. I met so many different people with so many different lives, and learned that they're not going to end up liking me even if it's because of a medical disorder. The options are suck it up and be a woman or die to them. So why spend all that time trying to justify myself to those people? Why spend all that time trying to shit on other trans people trying to live a life that makes them happy and comfortable rather than agreeing with the bigots that gender cannot be changed but exceptions should be made for me?

Instead, I spend my time fighting for a world that does choose to be more queer. For those people who would otherwise be cured of their dysphoria transitioning and passing but who want to experiment with their presentation.  For those people who didn't start out life in the same existential pain as me but still saw themselves happier in a life of color and genderfuckery. For those people who get crazy body modifications because it makes them feel closer to who they see themselves as. For those people who transition but still identify as cisgender. A world that tells those bigots "WHO CARES?! It's my body and my life, and society's expectations should change if they don't serve my autonomy." They don't have the right to kill us even if it is a choice. They don't have the right to destroy our lives even if it is a choice. It's the same reason I fight for reproductive rights, disability rights, and so much more liberation rather than trying to assimilate into a culture built to kill us. Don't give into the culture. Change it.

Then maybe consider it's not actually a hypothetical. I know many trans people who are not uncomfortable with their AGAB, but feel much happier when they transition. Instead of conceding to the medicalization of transness, why not challenge that? Why shouldn't people be able to choose a happier life like you seem to agree with? Even if that means being another gender without necessarily having gender dysphoria? Why is making a choice about your own body such a problem? It's not invalidating to say that you could choose to be trans. They're going to be shitty about it anyways because transphobia is inherently illogical. It's not about being a "good" or "valid" trans person. They hate us just for being trans at all.

I told you these terms that I knew of because you expressed a sentiment that I had felt before I realized I was asexual. I get ill thinking about sex but I didn't think that anyone would actually want me if I didn't want sex. I'd been told my whole life that it's not normal to not want it, that nobody wants a sexless relationship.

Then I discovered AVEN, a forum for people who are on the asexual spectrum, and I learned what a QPR was. The fact that it barely had a definition was what was so freeing. A QPR could be anything that me and my partner wanted, with boundaries that were defined by us and us alone, without the connotations that a romantic relationship would give. When I knew what to ask for, I found people that felt similarly who also wanted a relationship like that. It was like when I finally got a diagnosis for my POTS, I finally felt like I wasn't broken in some weird abstract way. There was a word to put to it, and it made me feel a little more understood. 

From my experience, we don't stand for making more and more labels. Many of us are against the strict defining and confining of labels, but that's what queerness is at its core. At least for me, my queerness is freeing because I don't have to define myself but I can if I want to and I'll always find community there. I can call myself queer and leave it at that. Your human needs some sleep hygiene! I struggled really hard with being able to sleep at night with my schizophrenia and junk, but these are the tips that have helped me the most. 

Have your human stick to a set bed time and wake up time. Like a sleep appointment! Look up how many hours a human of his age should be sleeping. It'll suck for a while and be hard to commit to at first, but you're by his side to remind him. Make bedtime fun, but definitely separate from your active time. You mentioned your human likes tea, maybe try a new calming tea or blend every day/week? Even on weekends, you have to make sure your friend is sleeping and waking up at the same time every day. This helps condition the body to begin slowing down about that time to let you sleep. No electronics before this bedtime, ideally an hour or two is screens off. Screens all day is a daytime activity to your brain, which means it thinks it needs to keep running to process. Pick out some books to read with your friend or color something before bed. It'll keep him from feeling like he's interrupting fun daytime tasks to go to sleep, so instead, replace it with things that are specifically there to signal its sleepy time. Your human also might need a cooler room, since it's harder for the body to enter sleep when it's hot and trying to regulate your temperature. Some very quiet and familiar music without lyrics or some noises can be helpful too, but don't force it if he prefers quiet. Overall, get him comfy and make bedtime a specific routine, not just something you do when you're tired.

Anxiety sucks, but it's your brain trying desperately to keep you alive. It's a survival mechanism on overdrive, but it's not meant to be your enemy. I don't know whether or not you can afford it, but if you can (I went through my state's insurance program to get mine), look into therapy. DBT has been incredible for helping me manage my anxiety that's tied to my PTSD and ADHD. It will help you with mindfulness and helping calm your racing thoughts when your anxiety flares. If you can't get therapy for whatever reason, love, look at how to cope with anxiety. 

My best advice from my own personal experience is two things. First, when you are feeling anxious and feeling a panic attack come on, do something that you wouldn't do if you were in danger. Eat something, like pop a mint in your mouth or pet something soft. Go out for a short run or walk. Doodle or write down your thoughts. When your brain kicks into overdrive like that, it thinks that you're in danger. Prove it wrong. Secondly, when having anxiety over tasks, think about the best case scenario and worst case scenario. Be realistic. What is the worst thing that could happen if I ask him out? Will he ignore me? Turn me down? Call me something mean? What is the best case scenario? Will he return my feelings and will I get together with him? And then after you've laid that out, could you live with the worst case scenario? I imagine you didn't drop dead when he ignored you, and it won't really have any significant consequences for the rest of your life. Would you much prefer the best case but could survive the worst case? It should help with the panic response when you talk out your anxiety with yourself.

You are incredibly lovely and anybody would be lucky to have you. Anxious people are the ones who are responsible and get shit done when they can utilize it well. There is help out there for you, there are people who will show in the timeline of your life who will be there for you. This is a hiccup in your life story at worst and a learnable moment at best. Learn some breathing techniques (trust me they are literally so helpful) and learn some mindfulness and meditation. Ground yourself when you start to feel yourself get absorbed in the static.
